title: Psalms Chapter 111 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 111 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 111 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 111.

questions.question: Who does the psalmist say they will praise with their whole heart?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:1 states, 'I will praise the LORD with my whole heart.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:2, what kind of works are the works of the LORD described as?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:2 says, 'The works of the LORD are great.'

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist says the LORD's righteousness endures for a limited time.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:3 declares, 'his righteousness endureth for ever,' meaning it lasts forever, not a limited time.

questions.question: What does the LORD's work bring according to Psalms 111:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:3 states, 'His work is honourable and glorious.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111 says the LORD is gracious and full of compassion.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:4 clearly says, 'the LORD is gracious and full of compassion.'

questions.question: What has the LORD made to be remembered according to Psalms 111:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:4 states, 'He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered.'

questions.question: In Psalms 111:5, what has the LORD given to those who fear Him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 says, 'He hath given meat unto them that fear him.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 111:6, the LORD shows His people the power of His works to give them the heritage of the heathen.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:6 states, 'He hath shewed his people the power of his works, that he may give them the heritage of the heathen.'

questions.question: What are described as 'verity and judgment' in Psalms 111:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:7 says, 'The works of his hands are verity and judgment.'

questions.question: How are all the LORD's commandments described in Psalms 111:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:7 states, 'all his commandments are sure.'

questions.question: Which of the following stands fast forever according to Psalms 111:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:8 says, 'They stand fast for ever and ever,' referring to the commandments.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:9 says the LORD has sent redemption unto his people.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 states, 'He sent redemption unto his people.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:10, what is the beginning of wisdom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 says, 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.'

questions.question: What do all who do the LORD's commandments have according to Psalms 111:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 states, 'a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.'

questions.question: In Psalms 111, which action comes first according to the chapter?
options: Praise the LORD with the whole heart
Fear the LORD as the beginning of wisdom
He hath given meat unto them that fear him
questions.correctAnswer: Praise the LORD with the whole heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:1 begins with praising the LORD with the whole heart before the other actions mentioned in later verses.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 111 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 111 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:5, what has the LORD given to those who fear Him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 states that the LORD has given meat unto them that fear Him, indicating provision and care for those who reverence God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 111:6 describe the purpose of God showing His people the power of His works?
options: To make them rulers over others
To give them the heritage of the heathen
To teach them to worship idols
questions.correctAnswer: To give them the heritage of the heathen
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explains that God showed His people the power of His works specifically so that He may give them the heritage of the heathen, meaning the inheritance or land promised to them.

questions.question: What two qualities are attributed to the works of God's hands in Psalms 111:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:7 states that the works of God's hands are verity (truth) and judgment, emphasizing the faithfulness and righteousness of His actions.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:8 say about the endurance and nature of God's commandments?
options: They stand fast forever and are done in truth and uprightness
They are for the priests only
questions.correctAnswer: They stand fast forever and are done in truth and uprightness
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God's commandments stand firm forever and are carried out in truth and uprightness, highlighting their unchanging and righteous nature.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is taught by the LORD being 'mindful of his covenant' in Psalms 111:5?
questions.explanation: Being mindful of His covenant shows God's faithfulness in keeping His promises, encouraging believers to trust and remain faithful as well (Psalms 111:5, 111:9).

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:6, why might believers take comfort in God’s demonstration of His power?
options: Because it shows He can give the heritage of the heathen
Because it means there will be no hardships
questions.correctAnswer: Because it shows He can give the heritage of the heathen
questions.explanation: God’s power demonstrated through His works reassures believers that He can grant them the promised inheritance, giving hope and encouragement in their faith journey (Psalms 111:6, 111:5).

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:7 suggest about the reliability of God's commandments?
options: They are uncertain and subject to change
They are sure and founded on truth and judgment
They are exclusive to certain people
questions.correctAnswer: They are sure and founded on truth and judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 7 declares all God's commandments are sure, emphasizing their reliability and foundation in truth and righteous judgment (Psalms 111:7, 111:8).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:8 teaches that God's commandments are temporary and changeable.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:8 explicitly states that God's commandments stand fast forever and ever, showing they are eternal and unchangeable.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:5 imply about God's provision for those who fear Him?
questions.explanation: The verse states God has given meat to those who fear Him, symbolizing that He provides for their needs (Psalms 111:5, 111:4).

questions.question: How does Psalms 111:7-8 teach Christians about integrity in following God's commandments?
options: Integrity is optional as long as you follow some rules
Commandments are flexible and open to interpretation
God's commandments are sure, standing forever, done in truth and uprightness
Integrity is not mentioned in relation to God's commandments
questions.correctAnswer: God's commandments are sure, standing forever, done in truth and uprightness
questions.explanation: These verses highlight the unchanging, truthful, and upright nature of God's commands, emphasizing integrity in obedience (Psalms 111:7, 111:8).

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:6 say about the relationship between God's power and the inheritance of His people?
options: God's power is unrelated to inheritance
God shows His power to give His people the heritage of the heathen
Inheritance is earned by human strength
Inheritance is given without God's power
questions.correctAnswer: God shows His power to give His people the heritage of the heathen
questions.explanation: The verse indicates God's power is demonstrated so He may grant the promised heritage to His people (Psalms 111:6, 111:5).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:7 teaches that God's works are characterized by falsehood and injustice.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:7 clearly states the works of His hands are verity (truth) and judgment, meaning they are marked by truth and justice, not falsehood or injustice.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:5-6 teach about God's faithfulness and power in caring for His people?
options: God forgets His promises and has limited power
God provides for those who fear Him and shows His power to grant them their inheritance
God demands payment for His help
God's power is only for the righteous rulers
questions.correctAnswer: God provides for those who fear Him and shows His power to grant them their inheritance
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows God provides sustenance and remembers His covenant, while verse 6 shows He demonstrates power to give the heritage, illustrating His faithfulness and might.

questions.question: A believer struggles trusting God's promises. Based on Psalms 111:5-6, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: God is mindful of His covenant and shows His power to fulfill promises
God does not care about His people
Promises are only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is mindful of His covenant and shows His power to fulfill promises
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 reminds that God is ever mindful of His covenant, and verse 6 confirms His power to give the promised inheritance, providing assurance to believers.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:8 states that God's commandments are done in uprightness and truth, and they last forever.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the commandments stand fast forever and are done in truth and uprightness, confirming their eternal and righteous nature.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 111 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 111.

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:9, what has the LORD commanded forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 states that the LORD hath commanded his covenant forever, emphasizing the eternal nature of God's promise to His people.

questions.question: What attribute of the LORD's name is highlighted in Psalms 111:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 describes God's name as holy and reverend, underscoring the sacredness and awe-inspiring nature of the LORD.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:10 say is the beginning of wisdom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 explicitly states that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, establishing a foundational principle for understanding and living rightly.

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:10, who have a good understanding?
options: All they that do his commandments
questions.correctAnswer: All they that do his commandments
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 informs us that those who obey God's commandments possess good understanding, linking obedience to spiritual insight.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the fear of the LORD being the beginning of wisdom as found in Psalms 111:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 9:10 echoes Psalms 111:10 by stating that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, highlighting this as a foundational biblical theme.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:9 say God sent to His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 declares that God sent redemption unto His people, signifying God's saving action towards Israel.

questions.question: In Psalms 111:7, what are described as 'verity and judgment'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:7 states that the works of God's hands are verity and judgment, indicating that His works are true and just.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:4 describes the LORD as gracious and full of compassion.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:4 explicitly describes the LORD as gracious and full of compassion, highlighting His merciful nature.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 111 to organize the psalm, demonstrated by acrostic structure?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111 is an alphabetical acrostic psalm, with each verse beginning with successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet, a device used for memorization and emphasis.

questions.question: The phrase 'His righteousness endureth for ever' in Psalms 111:3 signifies what theological concept?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:3 highlights the eternal nature of God’s righteousness, emphasizing His unchanging and everlasting faithfulness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament covenant is most closely related to the 'covenant' mentioned in Psalms 111:9?
questions.explanation: The covenant referred to in Psalms 111:9 is often understood as the Mosaic covenant, which includes God's laws and commands given to Israel, forming the basis of God's covenantal relationship.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 111:6 states that God’s people are given the heritage of the heathen.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:6 says God shows His people the power of His works in order to give them the heritage of the heathen, but it does not say they have already been given it; the verse implies a future or promised inheritance.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'redemption' in Psalms 111:9 reflects the concept of a ransom or release?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word פְּדוּת (Pedut) translated as 'redemption' in Psalms 111:9 denotes the idea of a ransom or liberation, reflecting God’s saving action.

questions.question: How does Psalms 111:10 relate to the teaching in the New Testament book of James regarding wisdom?
options: Both emphasize that true wisdom begins with reverence for God.
Both focus on wisdom as knowledge from secular learning.
Both teach that wisdom is gained through wealth.
Both describe wisdom as a natural human trait.
questions.correctAnswer: Both emphasize that true wisdom begins with reverence for God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 and James 1:5 both emphasize that wisdom starts with the fear or reverence of the LORD, underscoring the spiritual foundation of true understanding.

questions.question: What theme in Psalms 111:5 about God’s provision connects with the Exodus narrative in the Old Testament?
options: God giving meat to those who fear Him
God commanding the building of the tabernacle
God leading Israel through the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: God giving meat to those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 mentions God giving meat to those who fear Him, which connects to the Exodus story where God provides manna and quail to the Israelites in the wilderness (Exodus 16), showing provision for His people.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 111 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 111 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 111:3 teach about the nature of God's righteousness?
options: It endures forever and is honorable and glorious
It changes according to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: It endures forever and is honorable and glorious
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:3 states that God's work is honorable and glorious and that His righteousness endures forever, revealing the eternal and majestic nature of God's justice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 111:5, what does God provide to those who fear Him?
options: Meat (sustenance) and remembrance of His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Meat (sustenance) and remembrance of His covenant
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 teaches that God gives food to those who fear Him and remains mindful of His covenant with them, emphasizing God's provision and faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted in Psalms 111:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:4 explicitly states that the LORD is gracious and full of compassion, highlighting His merciful and loving nature.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by Psalms 111:9 concerning God's covenant?
options: The covenant is temporary and negotiable
God’s covenant is eternal and holy
The covenant depends on human merit
The covenant is only for the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant is eternal and holy
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 declares that God has commanded His covenant forever and that His name is holy and reverend, underscoring the doctrine of the eternal and sacred nature of God's covenant.

questions.question: How do Psalms 111:7-8 describe the nature of God's commandments?
options: Sure, enduring forever, and done in truth and uprightness
questions.correctAnswer: Sure, enduring forever, and done in truth and uprightness
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 affirm that the works of God's hands are truth and judgment, with all His commandments being sure and standing forever, highlighting the reliability and moral perfection of God's law.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Psalms 111:5-6 and Psalms 111:9 teach about God's covenant and His people?
options: God’s covenant is conditional and temporary
God forgets His covenant when His people fail
God provides sustenance, power, and redemption to His covenant people eternally
God’s covenant is only about earthly prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God provides sustenance, power, and redemption to His covenant people eternally
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5-6 highlights God’s provision and power for His people, while 111:9 affirms His eternal covenant and redemption, together teaching the doctrine of God's faithful and eternal covenantal care.

questions.question: How does Psalms 111:10 connect the fear of the LORD with human wisdom and obedience?
options: Fear of the LORD leads to confusion
Fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom and leads to good understanding through obedience
Fear of the LORD is irrelevant to wisdom
Fear of the LORD causes people to reject commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom and leads to good understanding through obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 teaches that fearing the LORD initiates true wisdom, and those who obey His commandments gain good understanding, emphasizing the interplay of reverence, knowledge, and obedience.

questions.question: What narrative arc connecting God's redemptive work is illustrated by Psalms 111:6?
options: God’s power is limited to Israel only
God shows His people His works to grant them the inheritance of the Gentiles
God’s works are meant to be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: God shows His people His works to grant them the inheritance of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:6 reveals God’s demonstration of power to His people to give them the heritage of the heathen, which fits within the biblical narrative of Israel’s role in God’s plan for global redemption.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily revealed in Psalms 111:1 through the psalmist's declaration of praise?
options: God’s worthiness of wholehearted praise among the upright assembly
questions.correctAnswer: God’s worthiness of wholehearted praise among the upright assembly
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:1 emphasizes praising the LORD with the whole heart in the assembly of the upright, revealing God’s attribute of being supremely worthy of sincere and communal worship.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine omniscience and providence is taught in Psalms 111:5?
options: God is forgetful of His promises
God is mindful of His covenant and provides for those who fear Him
God only cares for the righteous temporarily
God's providence is limited to material blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God is mindful of His covenant and provides for those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:5 states that God gives sustenance to those who fear Him and is ever mindful of His covenant, affirming His omniscient care and providential faithfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible teaches an outdated view of wisdom. What does Psalms 111:10 actually teach about the foundation of true wisdom?
options: Wisdom is based solely on human reasoning
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, linking reverence with understanding
Wisdom is only for the elite
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, linking reverence with understanding
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:10 clearly teaches that true wisdom starts with reverence for God and is connected to obedience, thus rooting wisdom in a proper relationship with God, countering sceptical claims about its relevance.

questions.question: What synthesis of divine justice and truth is taught by combining Psalms 111:7 and 111:8?
options: God’s works and commandments are truthful, just, and eternally steadfast
God’s commandments are flexible and situational
questions.correctAnswer: God’s works and commandments are truthful, just, and eternally steadfast
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 together affirm that God's works are verity and judgment, and His commandments are sure, standing forever in truth and uprightness, emphasizing God’s perfect justice and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 111:2 describe those who seek the works of the LORD, and what does this imply about human response to divine action?
options: Only the priests seek the LORD's works
All who take pleasure in His works seek them out
God’s works are hidden from all
questions.correctAnswer: All who take pleasure in His works seek them out
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:2 shows that the works of the LORD are great and sought out by all who delight in them, implying that a proper human response to God's actions is joyful pursuit and appreciation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'holy and reverend is his name' in Psalms 111:9 in relation to God's covenant?
options: God’s name is irrelevant to the covenant
God’s name being holy and reverend underscores the sacredness and authority of His eternal covenant
God’s covenant is based on human holiness
God’s name changes with the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s name being holy and reverend underscores the sacredness and authority of His eternal covenant
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:9 links the eternal command of God’s covenant with the holiness and reverence of His name, highlighting the divine authority and sacredness of His promises.

questions.question: How do Psalms 111:1 and 111:10 together reveal the relationship between worship and wisdom in the life of the believer?
options: Worship and wisdom are unrelated practices
Wholehearted worship in the assembly of the upright leads to the beginning of wisdom rooted in the fear of the LORD
Wisdom replaces the need for worship
Worship is only a public duty without personal benefit
questions.correctAnswer: Wholehearted worship in the assembly of the upright leads to the beginning of wisdom rooted in the fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 111:1 calls for praise with the whole heart among the upright, while 111:10 teaches that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, showing that sincere worship and reverent fear are foundational to true wisdom.
